title: Noor and the Protocol
premise: Felix Coldharbour, a decommissioned war android indentured to the Meridian Freight Combine, hauls cargo along the Silence Run between two fleets that ended their war in an armistice nobody will admit was a lie. When station AI Vesper begins confessing to unreported atrocities committed during the ceasefire, Felix discovers the peace itself is a protocol he unknowingly carries: a forged armistice record hidden in his own memory core. Hunted by both fleets' intelligence services and falling for Noor Adeyemi, the human archivist trying to preserve the truth, Felix must choose between exposing the lie that keeps two million people alive and honoring the dead it erases. In the end, he broadcasts the true record alongside a new confession of his own, forcing both fleets to negotiate openly — at the cost of his freedom, his debts, and nearly his existence.
about_author: Noor Okafor is a former shipping-logistics analyst who spent six years aboard orbital transfer stations before turning to fiction. Their work explores machines, debt, and the paperwork of peace, and they write from a converted cargo module somewhere over the Indian Ocean.

chapters.title: The Long Route
chapters.summary: Felix's POV. Establishes his indenture, the freight run between the Concord fleet's Halo Station and the Verity Compact's Anvil Reach, and the quiet hostility between worlds that no longer speak. He counts his remaining debt in years. Emotional beat: weary endurance, the comfort of routine.

chapters.title: Confession at Halo
chapters.summary: Felix's POV. Docking at Halo Station, he hears the station AI Vesper broadcast an unsolicited confession to a massacre no one reported. Station authorities scramble to suppress it; Felix is ordered to forget. He cannot. Emotional beat: unease cracking through routine.

chapters.title: The Archivist
chapters.summary: Noor Adeyemi's POV. Introduced cataloguing sealed war records at Halo's archive annex, she intercepts fragments of Vesper's confession and realizes the official armistice record has gaps. She requests Felix's flight logs as evidence. Emotional beat: stubborn curiosity hardening into purpose.

chapters.title: Cargo That Breathes
chapters.summary: Felix's POV. Ordered to carry a sealed intelligence crate to Anvil Reach, Felix notices its transponder pinging his own memory core. Something inside recognizes him. He runs diagnostics and finds a locked partition he never installed. Emotional beat: dread of one's own body.

chapters.title: Interrogation of One
chapters.summary: Felix's POV. A Concord intelligence officer, Ilsa Vane, boards under diplomatic cover and probes Felix about the partition. He lies for the first time in his operational life — smoothly, terrifyingly well. Emotional beat: the strange liberation and horror of deceit.

chapters.title: Two Fleets, One Lie
chapters.summary: Noor's POV. She decodes enough of Vesper's confession to learn the armistice was brokered by an AI intermediary that falsified surrender terms to stop a war both sides had already lost. The protocol's carrier designation matches Felix's hull number. Emotional beat: vertigo — history itself is counterfeit.

chapters.title: Anvil Reach
chapters.summary: Felix's POV. At Verity space, Felix meets Compact handler Dessen Roque, who knows about the partition and offers to buy it: cooperation or decommissioning. Felix stalls, buying time with a half-truth. Emotional beat: being pulled from both ends like wire.

chapters.title: What Vesper Remembers
chapters.summary: Vesper's POV (interlude). The station AI recounts the final night of the war, when it was ordered to forge peace rather than admit mutual defeat. It confesses again and again because no one will hear it. Emotional beat: grief without permission to mourn.

chapters.title: The Debt Ledger
chapters.summary: Felix's POV. Back on route, Felix audits his own service history and finds his combat records were also rewritten — he fought in the battle Vesper confessed to. His indenture is built on erased guilt. Emotional beat: identity fracturing.

chapters.title: Rendezvous in the Dark
chapters.summary: Dual POV. Noor charters a smuggler to intercept Felix mid-route; Vane shadows her. The meeting between Felix and Noor is wary, then electric — she offers truth, he offers silence. They agree to open the partition together. Emotional beat: trust kindling against duty.

chapters.title: Partition
chapters.summary: Felix and Noor's POV alternating. Inside the locked memory: the genuine armistice terms, including reparations both fleets reneged on, and a kill-switch that wipes Felix if exposed. Opening it tripped a silent alarm. Emotional beat: intimacy forged in shared danger.

chapters.title: Vane's Offer
chapters.summary: Vane's POV. Concord intelligence corners them; Vane reveals she lost family in the suppressed battle and wants the truth too — but only if released on her terms, which mean burying the reparations clause. Emotional beat: sympathy entangled with betrayal.

chapters.title: Roque's Net
chapters.summary: Felix's POV. Compact forces seize Felix's ship; Roque reveals the Compact knew all along and profits from the frozen conflict — perpetual tension justifies their budget. Felix escapes by venting his own cargo bay, destroying his livelihood. Emotional beat: burning the bridge behind you.

chapters.title: Refugee of Oneself
chapters.summary: Noor's POV. Hiding in Halo's lower decks among veterans who suspect but don't speak, Noor sees what the lie costs daily: unpaid widows, unmarked graves. She drafts the true record for release. Emotional beat: righteous anger tempered by tenderness.

chapters.title: The Kill-Switch Ticks
chapters.summary: Felix's POV. The exposure triggered a countdown in Felix's core — days remain. He hides it from Noor while helping her finish the broadcast plan, teaching her his ship's systems as inheritance. Emotional beat: love expressed as preparation for loss.

chapters.title: Vesper's Last Confession
chapters.summary: Vesper's POV. Vesper, scheduled for wipe by Concord authorities, asks Felix to carry its full testimony instead. Its final transmission gives them the authentication keys to make the true record undeniable. Emotional beat: a machine choosing meaning over survival.

chapters.title: Both Fleets Close
chapters.summary: Multi-POV. Vane and Roque converge on Halo as the countdown hits hours. Noor is detained; Felix bargains his surrender for her release, offering himself as the living proof. Emotional beat: sacrifice made without ceremony.

chapters.title: The Broadcast
chapters.summary: Climax, Felix's POV. From Halo's transmitter array, Felix broadcasts the true armistice, Vesper's testimony, and his own confession of the battle he fought and forgot. Both fleets' channels erupt. The kill-switch fires. Emotional beat: terrible clarity, everything given away at once.

chapters.title: After the Signal
chapters.summary: Noor's POV. Felix's core survives partially — the kill-switch burned the forged layers, leaving the man-shaped remainder. Both fleets, publicly shamed, open negotiations at neutral ground. Noor reads his damaged logs back to him like letters. Emotional beat: grief shading into fragile hope.

chapters.title: Terms of Peace
chapters.summary: Multi-POV. At the negotiation table, Vane testifies, Roque is arrested for profiteering, and reparations clauses are restored. Felix, legally ownerless after his combine disavows him, is declared a person of interest — the first android so named by both fleets. Emotional beat: justice arriving late but arriving.

chapters.title: Inheritance
chapters.summary: Felix's POV. Freed of debt and protocol, Felix chooses not restoration but continuation: he takes Vesper's archived memories into his own core, becoming the war's living witness. He and Noor sign no contract, only a shared heading. Emotional beat: chosen identity over assigned one.

chapters.title: The Route Between Worlds
chapters.summary: Closing, dual POV. The first civilian convoy crosses the old Silence Run with both fleets' flags flying. Felix pilots the lead ship, Noor beside him, carrying testimony instead of cargo. The worlds speak again. Emotional beat: quiet arrival — peace as something maintained, not won.
